title: Champagne Tower
summary: We stack glasses in a pyramid where the first row contains 1 glass, and each subsequent row contains one more glass than the row above it, up to 100 rows.
statement: We stack glasses in a pyramid where the first row contains 1 glass, and each subsequent row contains one more glass than the row above it, up to 100 rows. When champagne is poured into the top glass, any excess champagne overflows equally to the two glasses directly below it. This process continues until the champagne either fills the glasses or spills to the floor. Given a certain number of cups of champagne poured, determine the amount of champagne in the j-th glass of the i-th row, where both i and j are 0-indexed.
constraints: Each full glass keeps one cup and splits overflow equally downward; return queried fill up to one.
hints: Only overflow beyond one cup reaches the next row, split equally between two children.
Simulate one row of volumes at a time.
For each value add max(0,(value-1)/2) to both children; cap only the final answer.
All incoming contributions are accumulated before the next row, matching simultaneous flow through the tower.
editorial: All incoming contributions are accumulated before the next row, matching simultaneous flow through the tower.

tests.explanation: One cup fills only the top glass, leaving this lower glass empty.
One overflow cup splits evenly, so the queried glass contains one half.
